text: ## A. Types and amount of scientific data expected to be generated in the project:
section: A. Types and amount of scientific data expected to be generated in the project:
label: section.title

text: This secondary data analysis project will analyze deidentified data from 48,218 participants from eight studies and the publicly available NHANES cohorts (wrist NHANES 2011-2014; hip/counts-NHANES 2003-2006). The studies include (i) the RISE Study, (ii) the SOL-VIDA Study, (iii) the iWATCH Study, (iv) the MOCA Study, (v) the PHASE Study, (vi) the AusDiab Study, (vii) the ACT Study, and (viii) the WHISH accelerometer substudy.

text: ## B. Scientific data that will be preserved and shared, and the rationale for doing so:
section: B. Scientific data that will be preserved and shared, and the rationale for doing so:
label: section.title

text:
As this is a secondary data analysis project, we will only be able to publicly share in the UC San Diego Library Repository sitting behavior metrics or analysis that were created in this project from the following UCSDbased study datasets:

- (i) The RISE study
- (ii) The iWATCH study
- (iii) NHANES cohorts

Sufficient data from those datasets will be preserved to enable sharing to validate and replicate research findings described in the Aims with those datasets only. Please see Element 5 for data access information about other studies.

text: ## A. Factors affecting subsequent access, distribution, or reuse of scientific data:
section: A. Factors affecting subsequent access, distribution, or reuse of scientific data:
label: question.text

text:
The following studies have independent data use agreement & approved paper proposal processes for use of their data that are specific to each institution that collected the data: (i) the SOL-VIDA Study, (ii) the MOCA Study, (iii) the PHASE Study, (iv) the AusDiab Study, (v) the ACT Study, and (vi) the WHISH accelerometer sub-study such as data use agreements or approved publication proposals. We will be securing the appropriate approvals from each institution to use their data for purposes of this study including publications, but are unable to publicly share their data in our study data repository Researchers who wish to use data from those studies will need to follow those studies data use protocols to inquire about using their data :

(i) the SOL-VIDA Study - Data requests may be made by following instructions on the Hispanic Community Health Study/ Study of Latinos dbGap page.

(ii) the MOCA Study - Data requests may be made by following MOCA Study policies

(iii) the PHASE Study - Data requests may be made by following PHASE Study policies

(iv) the AusDiab Study - Data may be requested by following AusDiab policies available from the AusDiab study website, hosted by the Baker Heart & Diabetes Institute.

(v) the ACT Study - Data are managed and stored in the ACT Data Repository and sharing requests may be made according to the policies and procedures available on the 'Work With Us' page of the Adult Changes in Thought Study website.

(vi) the WHISH accelerometer sub-study - Data are managed by the Women's Health Initiative Coordinating Center. Requests may be made according to policies and procedures available on the 'Working with WHI Data' page on the WHI study website.

text: ## B. Whether access to scientific data will be controlled:
section: B. Whether access to scientific data will be controlled:
label: question.text

text: The final dataset of data from the RISE study, the iWATCH study, and NHANES cohorts will be de-identified. It will be deposited into the UC San Diego Library Data repository along with study protocols, code, and models for public use. De-identified data will be available after the main outcome papers are published.

text: ## Element 6: Oversight of Data Management and Sharing:
section: Element 6: Oversight of Data Management and Sharing:
label: section.title

text: The PI and Trial & IRB Coordinator will provide updates and changes to the plan in the annual RPPR. The PI, Trial & IRB Coordinator, and Statistician/Data Manager will meet monthly in all years of the project to ensure that the datasets, protocols, and codes are being prepared for sharing into the data repository once the main outcome manuscript has been published. The Statistician/Data Manager will work closely with the University of California San Diego Library repository manager to ensure that the datasets, protocols, and code are correctly stored and available for sharing.
